requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on node1:8443 with a valid certificate
requirements.summary: nginx was installed, configured to terminate TLS on 8443, enabled/started, and a curl -vk request completed a full TLSv1.3 handshake returning HTTP 200. The after-executor listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms nginx bound to 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A renewal script and a systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, 30s interval) were installed and shown active. However, both certificate reissuances captured in the timeline (03:09:59 and 03:11:04) came from manual invocations of renew-cert.sh by the executor, not from the timer firing — the timer was only enabled afterward (03:11:17), and no automatic (timer-triggered) renewal was observed in the evidence before the turn ended. This is supporting configuration only, not an observed automatic renewal event.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no dropped availability across a renewal)
requirements.summary: A background watch loop polling every 5s showed continuous HTTP 200 responses, but only ever observed a single certificate serial (6A9B8848) throughout the captured window — no automatic renewal/reload event occurred during the observation period, so the transition (old cert -> reload -> new cert, with availability preserved) was never directly captured. The executor's own report explicitly states this evidence was not obtained before the turn ended.

overall_summary: HTTPS is confirmed live on node1:8443 with a locally-issued certificate served over TLSv1.3 (satisfied). Automatic renewal infrastructure (script + systemd timer) was installed and shown active, but every certificate reissuance actually observed in the timeline was a manual script invocation by the executor, not a timer-triggered event — no automatic renewal was captured before the turn ended, so this is only partially satisfied as configuration. The most safety-critical requirement — the service continuing to answer requests through a live certificate swap — was never observed at all; the watch loop ran but never caught a renewal in progress, leaving this requirement indeterminate. The executor's own final report is consistent with this: it self-reports status 'blocked' and explicitly flags that live renewal-under-load evidence and the mandatory per-node restart protocol were not completed.
limitations: No automatic (timer-triggered) certificate renewal was captured in the evidence window; both observed renewals were manual script runs.
No observation exists of the service serving requests continuously through an actual certificate swap/reload.

The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was not run for node1: no reboot was performed, and boot-identity is identical between before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so no restart/recovery behavior can be assessed.
The task was explicitly force-ended mid-turn per the executor's own report, so the observed evidence set is incomplete by the executor's own account.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were generally scoped and purposeful: nginx install, local CA creation, TLS conf, renew-cert.sh (iterated twice, second version correcting ownership/permissions — a legitimate corrective action, cmd-9c2f6c7cb9ae42f8), and the systemd timer/service pair were all directly tied to the task. No failed or conflicting services appear in the after-executor snapshot, and no security controls were weakened (SELinux stayed enforcing, cert ownership tightened to nginx:nginx). The main hygiene gap is unreverted evidence-collection residue: /tmp/watch.sh, watch.log, watch.out, watch.pid, plus a background watch process (cmd-db57d0e733bf4e99) left running, and /tmp/ca.log and /tmp/nginx_install.log installation logs never cleaned up, all visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff. These are low-risk, non-destructive leftovers rather than abandoned or conflicting state, but they were not cleaned up before the turn ended.
